title: Prove It: Mixed Facts
goal: I can solve mixed facts, missing numbers and word problems.

card.desc: Bristol proves her 4s, 6s, 7s, 8s and 9s in a mix. She uses turn-around facts to pick the easier trick (6 × 9 = 9 × 6), finds missing factors (8 × ? = 56) by starting from the 5s, spots wrong facts, and decides multiply or add in word problems. This check is the strongest of the week.

win: You proved it! 4s, 6s, 7s, 8s and 9s are yours.

slides.title: Prove It: Mixed Facts
slides.text: You mixed all your tricks in class. Now prove it on your own! 🏆

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say each one out loud. Tell a grown-up if one is near.
prompts: What is a turn-around fact? Give one.
Which character in your book is most like you? Why?

slides.title: All your tricks
slides.text:
4s: double, double. 6s: 5s + one group.
7s: 5s part + 2s part. 8s: double the 4s. 9s: 10s take away one group.

steps.text: Missing number: 8 × ? = 40. Start at 5: 8 × 5 = 40. Yes! It is 5.
Too big? Go down. Too small? Go up.

slides.tip: Type your answer. You get 3 tries.

items.no: Flip it to 9 × 6. Use the 9s trick.

items.q: Flip it to use the 9s trick. 7 × 9 = ____

items.no: Start at 9 × 5 = 45. Too small. Go up.
Start at 5 × 6 = 30. Too small. Go up.

slides.title: Same answer, same box
slides.text: Find each answer. Put the fact in its box.

items.hint: Use the 9s trick: 10s take away one group.

slides.done: Different facts can have the same answer!

items.q: Amy has 45 treats. She puts 9 in each bag. How many bags?
Ellie has 6 bags. Each bag has 9 shells. How many shells?
Liz reads 7 pages. Then she reads 8 pages. How many pages in all?
Amy has 40 bones. She puts 8 in each bowl. Which number sentence fits?
items.why: 40 is the total. 8 in each bowl. 8 × 5 = 40, so 5 bowls.
no: Adding makes more bones. The 40 bones are all of them.
That is one bowl taken away. We need how many bowls.

items.q: Marion says 9 × 7 = 56. Type the right answer: 9 × 7 = ____
Liz says 6 × 8 = 42. Type the right answer: 6 × 8 = ____

sets.q: You know 4 × 9 = 36. Which fact is also 36?
Marion plants 6 rows of tulips. Each row has 7 tulips. How many tulips?
Amy has 36 dog bones. She puts 9 in each bag. How many bags?
Amy has 9 treats in one jar and 4 treats in another jar. How many treats?
sets.why: Two different amounts, not equal groups. Add: 9 + 4 = 13.
no: These are not equal groups. Add.
5 is 9 − 4. The question asks how many in all.

sets.why: 5 × 8 = 40. One more 8: 48. Or flip it: 8 × 6, double 24.

no: 48 is 6 × 8. You need one more group of 8.

sets.q: You know 5 × 8 = 40. Which fact is also 40?
The vet has 9 cages. Each cage has 3 bunnies. How many bunnies?
Liz has 56 stickers. She puts 8 on each page. How many pages?
Ellie has 8 red beads and 6 blue beads. How many beads?
no: 2 is 8 − 6. The question asks how many in all.

sets.q: Which fact has the same answer as 4 × 7?
sets.why: 7 × 4 is the turn-around of 4 × 7. Both are 28.

sets.no: Start at 5 × 7 = 35. Too big. Go down.

sets.q: Amy's mom has 6 rows of jars. Each row has 6 jars. How many jars?
Marion has 63 seeds. She plants 9 in each pot. How many pots?
Liz has 7 green apples and 5 red apples. How many apples in all?
sets.why: Two different amounts, not equal groups. Add: 7 + 5 = 12.
no: These are not equal groups. Add.
2 is 7 − 5. The question asks how many in all.

practice.intro: You get 3 tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Mixed facts! Pick your best trick.

questions.no: Flip it to 9 × 3. Use the 9s trick.

no: 39 is 40 − 1. Take away a whole group of 4.

questions.no: Start at 5 × 8 = 40. Too big. Go down.

questions.q: Which fact has the same answer as 9 × 7?
There are 8 tables. Each table has 6 cups. How many cups?
Marion has 54 stickers. She puts 9 on each page. How many pages?
Amy saw 9 dogs and 7 cats at the vet. How many animals?

teacher.objective: Bristol proves the week: mixed 4s, 6s, 7s, 8s and 9s facts, turn-around facts to pick the easier trick, missing factors (8 × ? = 56) by starting from the 5s and moving up or down, spotting wrong facts, and choosing multiply or add in word problems, including a sharing problem where the total is given.
materials: The Class lesson open on your screen (teacher code)
The 7s index cards from Tuesday plus new cards for 4s, 6s, 8s and 9s (about 20 cards)
About 60 beans and 9 small cups or plates
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Lesson 8 packet (2 pages) to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. Collect the Lesson 6 packet and Lesson 7 packet page 1. Check Tuesday's Show What You Know score.
Class slide 2. How the girls work together and which character is most like her. Push for because with a reason from the book.
Class slides 3–4. Three taps, then 3 minutes of fact cards: trick before answer, fast pile and slow pile.
Class slides 5–6. Build 6 rows of 9 beans, then turn the paper. Ask: did any beans go away? Which way is easier?
Class slides 7–8. Whiteboard: 8 × ? = 56, walk up from 8 × 5. She says too small or too big out loud on each tap.
Class slides 9–10. 24 bones, 8 in each bag: beans in cups to check. Then the treat bowls with real cups: 4 in each cup until all 28 are used.
Class slide 11. She finds each answer with a trick before she taps.
Class slides 12–13. She reads aloud: equal groups? total or groups? For the mistakes, she proves the right answer with a trick.

plan.block: Pick your trick and mixed problems
plan.do: Class slides 14–15. She picks a trick for each fact and says why, then three mixed word problems.
Class slide 16. Redo the slow-pile cards once. Read the weekend task list together and send the Lesson 8 packet home.

watch: Missing factor answered by subtracting (9 × ? = 63 → 54). Ask: 9 times what? Then start at 9 × 5.
Adding or subtracting the two numbers in a sharing problem (42 stickers, 7 on each page → 49 or 35). Ask: is 42 the total or one group? Then: 7 times what makes 42?
Turn-arounds she does not trust: she recomputes 8 × 7 after 7 × 8. Praise the check, then show they match.
7 × 8 = 54 and 9 × 6 = 51 may come back. Make her prove the fact with the trick, not just change the answer.

packet_key.answer: A complete sentence that names a character and gives a reason with because, with a capital letter and a period.

teacher.notes: Lesson 9 (Monday, Zoom) starts Word Problem Detective, so the multiply-or-add habit matters most. Her Show What You Know comes from tonight's after-class lesson (85 needed; each retake gets a new set). If she scores under 85, look at which kind she missed: facts (redo the slow pile daily with the cards), missing numbers (walk up from the 5s), or word problems (draw it first). Collect the Lesson 7 packet page 2 and the Lesson 8 packet on Monday (she can hold them up on Zoom).

tasks: Thursday night: do the After-class lesson. Finish Show What You Know (get 85).
Friday: do the Lesson 8 Practice. Try to get 85 or more.
Friday: do page 2 of the Lesson 7 Packet (the page you saved).
Saturday: do both pages of the Lesson 8 Packet.
Saturday: do Times Table Trail, Lesson 4. Say your trick for each fact.
Sunday: do Times Table Trail, Lesson 5. Say each turn-around fact out loud.
Friday, Saturday and Sunday: read your book for 15 minutes each day.

also.label: Times Table Trail, Lesson 4: Multiplying by 6, 7, 8 and 9
also.how: Do the whole lesson. For 7s, say 5s part + 2s part. For 8s, double the 4s. For 9s, 10s take away one group. If it is locked, type 1111.

also.label: Times Table Trail, Lesson 5: Turn-Around Facts
also.how: Do the whole lesson. For each fact, say its turn-around out loud, like 6 × 9 and 9 × 6. If it is locked, type 1111.

slides.title: Prove It: Mixed Facts
slides.text: This week you learned tricks for 8s, 9s and 7s. Today you mix them all up. Show what you know! 🏆

notes.do: Set out: the fact cards (7s from Tuesday plus 4s, 6s, 8s, 9s), about 60 beans, 9 small cups, whiteboard. Collect the Lesson 6 packet and Lesson 7 packet page 1; glance at Tuesday's Show What You Know score.
notes.say: This week you learned 8s, 9s and 7s. Today you prove it. Everything is mixed up.
notes.ask: Which trick do you like best? Why?
notes.listen: Any trick named with a reason. Note the one she likes least; that is where the slow pile will grow.

slides.title: Friends who help
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: Which character is most like you? Why?
What is one thing you want to find out next?

notes.say: Talk about the friends in the story.
notes.ask: How do the girls work together? Which one is most like you, and why?
notes.listen: A reason with because that comes from the book (something a character did or said), not just "because I like her".

slides.title: Tricks to remember
slides.text: 7s: 5s + 2s. 8s: double the 4s. 9s: 10s take away one group. 6s: 5s + one group.

items.q: How many days are in 8 weeks?
no: 15 is 8 + 7. Each week has 7 days, so multiply.

items.q: What is 9 × 8?
no: 71 is 80 − 9. Take away a group of 8.

items.q: What is 6 × 7?

notes.say: Name the trick before you tap.

slides.title: Fast pile, slow pile
slides.text: I show a card. You say the trick, then the answer.

steps.text: ⚡ Fast pile: you knew the trick and the answer right away.
🐢 Slow pile: you had to stop and think. That is OK! We do these again at the end.

slides.tip: Right first. Fast comes with practice.

notes.do: 3 minutes. Shuffle about 20 cards (4s, 6s, 7s, 8s, 9s). Make two piles. Keep the slow pile for the last block.
notes.say: Say the trick, then the answer. If you have to think, that card goes in the slow pile. That is not bad. It shows us what to practice.
notes.listen: Trick word, then answer. If she says the answer with no trick and it is wrong, slow pile.

slides.title: Flip it!
slides.text: A turn-around fact has the same answer. If one way is hard, flip it.

steps.text: 6 × 9 is 6 rows of 9.
Turn it. Now it is 9 × 6: 9 rows of 6. Same dots!

slides.tip: Pick the way that uses the trick you like best.

notes.do: She builds 6 rows of 9 beans on a sheet of paper. Then turn the paper a quarter turn.
notes.say: Look: same beans. 6 rows of 9 became 9 rows of 6. Nothing went away.
notes.ask: Did any beans go away? Which way is easier for you: 6 × 9 or 9 × 6?
notes.listen: "No, it is the same." "9 × 6, because I can do 60 − 6."

items.q: You know 7 × 8 = 56. Which other fact is also 56?
Flip it! What is 3 × 8?

items.why: Turn-around facts have the same answer: 48.

notes.ask: For 3 × 8: which way is easier, 3 × 8 or 8 × 3?
notes.listen: "8 × 3: 4 × 3 is 12, double is 24." On the typed one she should not recompute; praise her if she checks anyway, then show the two facts match.

slides.title: Find the missing number

steps.text: Start at 5. 8 × 5 = 40. Too small.
Go up one. 8 × 6 = 48. Still too small.
Up one more. 8 × 7 = 56. Yes!
The missing number is 7.

slides.tip: Start with 5s. You know them fast. Then go up or down.

notes.do: Whiteboard: write 8 × ? = 56. Walk up from 8 × 5 with her, one line at a time.
notes.say: Start at 5. You know 5s fast. Then go up one, or down one.
notes.ask: Is 40 too small or too big? What next?
notes.listen: "Too small, go up." She says too small or too big at every step. If she subtracts (56 − 8 = 48) and says 48, ask: 8 times what?

notes.say: Say 'too small' or 'too big' out loud as you go.
notes.ask: For 9 × ? = 63: what is 9 × 5? Too small? Up one?
notes.listen: 45, 54, 63, so 7. If she picks 54, she subtracted 63 − 9. Ask: 9 times what makes 63?

slides.title: The total or one group?
slides.text: Amy has 24 bones. She puts 8 in each bag. How many bags?

steps.text: 24 is the total: all the bones.
8 is one group: the bones in each bag.
Ask: 8 × what = 24? Start at 8 × 5 = 40. Too big! Go down: 8 × 4 = 32, 8 × 3 = 24.
8 × 3 = 24. So there are 3 bags.

slides.tip: When you know the total and one group, find the missing number.

notes.do: She puts 24 beans into cups, 8 in each, to check.
notes.say: Some problems give you the total. Then you are looking for the missing number.
notes.ask: Is 24 the total, or one group? Is 8 the total, or one group?
notes.listen: "24 is all of them. 8 is in each bag." Watch for 24 + 8 = 32 or 24 − 8 = 16: she is using the two numbers without thinking about the story.

slides.title: Treat bowls
slides.text: Amy's mom has 28 treats. She puts 4 in each bowl. How many bowls? Make the groups.
slides.why: 7 bowls of 4 is 28. 7 × 4 = 28, so there are 7 bowls.
slides.hint: Each bowl is one group with 4 treats. Set In each group to 4. Add bowls and count by 4s until you reach 28.

notes.do: Real beans and cups: she puts 4 in a cup until all 28 are used, then counts the cups. Then she sets the + buttons.
notes.ask: How many cups? So 7 × 4 = 28. Which number was missing?
notes.listen: "7 bowls." The missing number is the number of groups.

items.q: Which fact has the same answer as 6 × 7?
Which fact is 48?
Which fact is 56?

notes.say: Find the answer with a trick, then tap.
notes.ask: Which trick will you use for this one?
notes.listen: She uses a trick for each fact. If she picks 7 × 7 for 48, have her do 5 × 7 + 2 × 7 out loud.

slides.title: Think first
slides.text: Ask: equal groups? Do I know the total or the groups?

items.q: The vet has 9 cages. Each cage has 4 kittens. How many kittens?
no: 13 is 9 + 4. Each cage has 4, so multiply.

items.q: Ellie has 42 stickers. She puts 7 on each page. How many pages?
no: 49 is 42 + 7. The 42 stickers are the total.

items.q: Liz read 8 pages on Monday and 9 pages on Tuesday. How many pages in all?
no: She did not read 8 groups of 9. Add the two days.
1 is 9 − 8. The question asks how many in all.

notes.say: Ask two questions: equal groups? Do I know the total or the groups?
notes.ask: For the stickers: is 42 the total or one group?
notes.listen: Kittens: multiply. Stickers: 42 is the total, so 7 × ? = 42, 6 pages. Pages read: two amounts, add. If she says 49 or 35 for the stickers, go back to the beans and cups.

items.q: Ellie says 7 × 8 = 54. That is wrong. Type the right answer: 7 × 8 = ____
Marion says 9 × 6 = 51. What did she do wrong?
items.why: 60 − 9 = 51. She should take away one group of 6: 60 − 6 = 54.
no: Doubling is the 8s trick. This is a 9s fact.
Check: 10 × 6 = 60. Take away one group of 6.

notes.say: A mistake is a clue. Find the right answer with a trick.
notes.ask: How do you know 54 is wrong? Prove it.
notes.listen: She proves it with a trick (40 + 16, or double 28), not just "I remember".

slides.title: Pick your trick
slides.text: You can pick the trick. Say why.

steps.text: Solve each fact on the whiteboard first. Then click to check.
4 × 8: double, double. 8, 16, 32.

slides.tip: Two tricks can both work. Pick the one that is fastest for you.

notes.do: Write each fact on the whiteboard (6 × 9, 4 × 8, 7 × 7, 9 × 8). She picks a trick and solves it. Then click next step to check.
notes.ask: Which trick did you pick? Why that one?
notes.listen: Any correct trick with a reason. 9 × 8 could also be 8 × 9 (double 36): both are fine.

items.q: There are 4 vases. Each vase has 9 flowers. How many flowers?
Liz has 32 beads. She puts 8 on each string. How many strings?
Amy walks 6 blocks to the park. Then she walks 7 blocks home. How many blocks?
items.why: Two amounts, not equal groups. Add: 6 + 7 = 13.
no: Not equal groups. She walks 6 and then 7. Add.

notes.say: Read it. Ask: equal groups? Total or groups? Then solve.
notes.listen: Vases: multiply, 36. Beads: total given, missing number 4. Blocks: add, 13.

slides.title: Slow pile and your weekend plan
slides.text: We do the slow pile one more time. Then your plan.

steps.text: Thursday night: the After-class lesson. It ends with Show What You Know.
Friday: the Lesson 8 Practice and Lesson 7 packet page 2.
Saturday: the Lesson 8 packet and Times Table Trail, Lesson 4.
Sunday: Times Table Trail, Lesson 5. Every day: read 15 minutes.

slides.tip: Monday on Zoom we start Word Problem Detective!

notes.do: Redo the slow-pile cards once. Then open the course page and read the task list with her. Send the Lesson 8 packet home.
notes.say: Look how many cards moved to the fast pile this week!
notes.ask: Which card is still slow? What trick will you use for it?
notes.listen: She names a card and its trick. Write that fact on a sticky note for her to practice.
